set.tovw: Found: the whole box was recovered in Nov 1900
set.st: Nov 1900: a farmer cutting a maple in his pasture between Lynn and Romadka found a decayed 2-ft wooden box at its base: 120 American and Mexican silver dollars (1846-59), about $200 in gold eagles and double eagles, pounds of old gold and silver watch cases, candlesticks and solid silver tableware. Nothing is said to remain. It recalled a farmer between Lynn and Romadka supposed murdered, robbed and his house burned some twenty years earlier (c.1880); a skeleton was found buried by the roadside near the spot in 1899. A neighbour was suspected but never charged. The farm is not on the 1893 Lynn, Fremont or York plats or the 1906 Lynn plat; Romadka is York sec. 24 (T25N R1W), so the pin sits at the midpoint of the roughly 3-mile rail corridor between Lynn and Romadka, not the spot itself.
set.pl: Rail corridor between Lynn and Romadka, Clark Co. (midpoint); the pasture is not yet placed
